Maya R: Quick sync — I sketched a compact autoscale control for the pool card. Need calls on three things: SLO slider granularity (1% vs 5%), how min/max number inputs accept keyboard entry, and the burst confirmation microcopy + accessibility. Sam K: Love the compact layout. Main thing: keyboard users need a way to nudge min/max without opening a modal. +/- keyboard shortcuts? Jules (FE): We can add focusable steppers with arrow-key increments. Current plan: stepper increments 1 by default, long-press to accelerate. For sliders, arrow keys +/- 1% each tick. Ravi P: For GPU pools we also need pool selector behavior when a pool is filtered out by policy. Should we show disabled option with tooltip or remove it entirely? Olivia T: Prefer disabled + tooltip: makes policy constraints discoverable. UX pattern: show reason text like “Reserved by security policy” and link to docs. Connor (a11y): A few a11y notes: 1) slider needs visible focus ring and aria-valuemin/valuemax/valuenow set. 2) Stepper buttons must have aria-labels ("increase min vcpus", "decrease min vcpus"). 3) Pool picker needs combobox semantics and should announce when selection is restricted. Maya R: Good call. For slider granularity: product leaning toward 5% for simplicity, but we risk losing fine SLO control. Thoughts? Sam K: 5% OK for most customers, but for latency-critical routes some teams want +/-1%. Could we show a small "precision" toggle (fine/coarse) when you click the numeric value? Jules (FE): Implementation note: toggling granularity can just change step attribute on the input. But the keyboard behaviour needs to swap step size too. Fine toggle could be an inline button next to the number. Ravi P: If we add fine mode, ensure API surface supports decimal SLO values and the console sends exact numbers in the rollout policy. Backend already handles floats but we should validate in UI. Maya R: OK. Next — burst confirmation modal copy. Current draft: \"Enable burst? This will allocate additional GPUs temporarily.\" Need clarity on duration and cost. Suggestions? Olivia T: Draft: \"Enable burst: temporarily allocates X additional GPUs for up to Y minutes. You will be billed for the burst capacity while active.\" Add a small link: "How burst billing works". Sam K: Also add a toggle for "auto-revert" vs "manual revert" — some teams want automatic cooldown. Copy: \"Auto-revert after the burst period\" with tooltip. Connor (a11y): Modal must be dismissible with Esc and should trap focus. The primary action button should be clearly labeled — avoid generic labels like "Confirm". Use: "Enable burst (X GPUs for Y min)". Also add aria-describedby referencing the billing explanation text. Jules (FE): Agree on explicit CTA. Code snippet for the CTA label we can use: ``` ``` Maya R: Nice. One more: pool picker combobox copy — when a pool has preemptible nodes, we currently show a tiny badge "preemptible". Design wants a stronger affordance: maybe a subtle warning state on selection and a recommended alternative. Ravi P: Show badge + an inline help link "Why this matters" that opens a tooltip explaining preemption risk and cost tradeoffs. If pool is recommended, show a green check and text "Recommended for latency-critical routes". Olivia T: Microcopy suggestion for warning: "This pool uses preemptible instances — workloads may be interrupted. Consider using a dedicated pool for strict SLOs." Keep it short. Connor (a11y): Add role=alert when we switch to a preemptible pool programmatically, so screen readers announce the change. Also ensure contrast of the badge meets AA. Maya R: Awesome. Action items: 1) Jules — implement slider step toggle and keyboard handling prototype (due EOD Thu). 2) Connor — provide exact aria attribute list and sample markup. 3) Olivia — finalize modal copy + billing link text. 4) Ravi — confirm API accepts decimal SLOs and edge cases. 5) Sam — mock up keyboard steppers and a11y focus flow. Sam K: Acked. I'll sketch the keyboard flows and post screenshots. Jules (FE): I'll throw together a quick CodePen for the slider + stepper behavior. Connor (a11y): Quick sample aria example for the slider to get started: ```html
``` Maya R: Perfect. If nobody objects I'll fold these into the next design pass and post updated comps. Thanks all :rocket: rollout-bot: New design pass uploaded: https://redwood.design/figma/compact-autoscale-v3 (uploaded by Maya R) :white_check_mark: Sam K: checking the figma now. Looks tight — will comment on the keyboard flow frames. Olivia T: small nit in figma: the fine/coarse toggle needs an accessible hit target (at least 44px). Jules (FE): noted. I'll increase tappable area and update the prototype. Maya R: Great — closing thread once prototypes are linked.
